idea/top: At the top, the model scores every token by multiplying the final stream by the unembedding: one row per token, one dot product each.
idea/sum: But the final stream is just x zero plus every block's write, and a partial sum is the same kind of vector.
idea/lens: So multiply the stream partway up by the same unembedding. That is the logit lens: what the model would predict if it stopped there.
example/setup: A tiny model reads "the capital of Italy is". Its stream is two numbers wide, and three tokens matter: Paris, Rome, and "the". Here is each token's row of the unembedding.
example/x0: The stream starts at one, zero. Dot it with each row: Paris scores two, Rome zero, "the" one. The lens says Paris.
example/x1: Block zero writes minus one, two, so the stream becomes zero, two. Now Paris scores zero, Rome four, and "the" two. After block zero, the lens says Rome.
example/story: Read block by block, the lens shows the answer forming. Early blocks also write notes for later ones that the unembedding cannot read, so early guesses are often noisy.
